text:
lucy: Heads-up — onboarding sample failing for several Windows users (py3.8-3.12). Async snippet raises: ssl.SSLCertVerificationError: [SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] unable to get local issuer certificate. The sync requests example works as-is.

omar: Is this the MS Store Python or python.org installer? They differ on how certs/openssl are wired.

lucy: python.org installers across Win10/11. certifi is installed but async still blows up.

pat: Two layers here: (1) httpx/anyio async path doesn't always respect REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE the way requests does, and (2) Windows default asyncio loop (Proactor) can expose socket/ssl combination bugs.

lucy: The error stack in logs is unhelpful — users just see ConnectionError in the SDK, no SSL detail. Makes triage slow.

omar: We should preserve exception chaining in our retry layer so the underlying SSLCertVerificationError isn't lost. Right now retry middleware wraps with a fresh RequestError w/o __cause__.

pat: Quick local workaround that fixed it for me on Win11: create an SSLContext pointing at certifi and pass it into the AsyncClient; also switch to the selector loop. Example I dropped into the sample:

```
import ssl
import certifi
import asyncio
from redwood import AsyncClient

ctx = ssl.create_default_context(cafile=certifi.where())
# selector loop avoids some proactor/socket interop issues on Windows
asyncio.set_event_loop_policy(asyncio.WindowsSelectorEventLoopPolicy())

async def demo():
    async with AsyncClient(ssl=ctx) as c:
        await c.chat("test")

asyncio.run(demo())
```

pat: That made the async flow use the same trust store as requests and avoid the verification failure locally.

lucy: Nice — but two related problems: our type stubs for AsyncClient don't expose the ssl kwarg so mypy users try verify=... and get confused, and samples/doc should surface the Windows note.

omar: Agreed. Action items: 1) update retry middleware to preserve original exception as __cause__, 2) add Optional[ssl.SSLContext] to AsyncClient typing/stubs, 3) update onboarding samples to include the Windows snippet + env var fallback, 4) add a lightweight Windows runner in GH Actions across py3.8-3.12 to catch regressions.

pat: I'll open a small PR covering 1 & 2 (retry chaining + typing). I'll also add a comment in the code to prefer certifi.where() on Windows if no ssl provided.

infra: Platform note — adding Windows matrix entries is fine but we prefer a single lightweight job that runs the async client basic smoke tests on 3.8, 3.11 and 3.12 to start; we can expand later.

lucy: OK cool. Filed issue 2599 to track this work: "windows-async-ssl-typing-ci-parity". devex-bot: created issue 2599.

devex-bot: Issue 2599 created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-sdk/issues/2599

omar: Also document parity: explicitly state that sync honors REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE / REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE env while async will honor SSLContext or SSL_CERT_FILE/certifi fallback — otherwise users will be surprised.

pat: If anyone still hits CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED after the PR, please paste full exception.__cause__ + python build details (store vs installer) and we'll follow up with a minimal repro. :+1:
